name: Ross's Goose
rangeDescription: Breeds tundra of arctic north-central canada; winters to western and central usa and central mexico
description: Cute miniature version of Snow Goose with smaller body, shorter neck, and stubbier bill. Pay special attention to the bill: short, with a straighter border where it meets the face, a much less obvious dark “grin patch,” and often bluish-gray color at the base.

name: Pink-footed Goose
rangeDescription: Breeds greenland, iceland, and spitsbergen; winters northwestern europe
description: Relatively small and short-necked goose with contrasting dark brown head and neck, small black bill with pink band near tip, and pink legs. In flight shows extensively pale silvery upperwings.

name: Böhm's Bee-eater
rangeDescription: Humid forest of southeastern africa (malawi and adjacent countries)
description: Slim green bee-eater with an orange throat and crown, a black tip to the tail, and elongated black tail streamers. Found very locally in moist woodland and forest edge, usually near rivers and streams.

name: Tiger Shrike
rangeDescription: Northeastern asia; winters to southeastern asia, greater sundas, and philippines
description: Small, short-tailed shrike with a heavy-headed appearance. Found in lowland forests, edges, and parks.

name: Chestnut-breasted Whiteface
rangeDescription: Elevated gibber plains of central south australia
description: Small bird with stubby bill, found in open shrubland in stony country of arid northeastern South Australia. Warm brown above, white below, with broad rusty-brown chest band, reddish-brown marks on the flanks, pale eye, grayish throat, and white mark above bill.

name: Raiatea Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Western society islands (bora bora, tahaa, huahine, and maupiti)
description: An unmistakable dove with a bright silver head, neck, and chest, dark green wings, a light green belly, and a yellowish tint to the forehead. Bill is bright banana yellow.

name: Puerto Rican Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Puerto rico including isla de culebra and isla de vieques (both just east of puerto rico), and virgin islands
description: An inconspicuous woodland species often first detected by voice. It has a slender build and is colored dull brown above and mostly grayish white below.

name: Somali Bunting
rangeDescription: Sudan to ethiopia, somalia, uganda, kenya, and northeastern tanzania
description: A beautiful bunting of dry country. Note the black-and-white facial pattern, the gray back with russet streaks, the gray rump, and the yellow breast with pale sides.

name: Venezuelan Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Coastal cordillera of northern venezuela (southern lara eastward to miranda)
description: Small, drab tyrannulet with limited range in northern Venezuela. Fairly inconspicuous; usually found as singles or pairs in middle to upper levels of forests, plantations, and second-growth.

name: Chinese Bamboo-Partridge
rangeDescription: Arid bush of southern and central china
description: While common in bamboo forest, this loud and colorful partridge can be found in a range of other shrubby and semiopen habitats. Not particularly shy; singing males can be located by their far-carrying song, a rising series of piercing single and triple notes.

name: Garganey
rangeDescription: Breeds palearctic (except north); winters to central africa through indonesia
description: Small and often rather unobtrusive duck of wetlands with reedy and other fringing vegetation. Handsome male distinctive, with big white eyebrow on dark brown head, pale gray flanks; pale gray forewing striking in flight.

name: Red-bellied Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Eastern north america (southern canada to texas and florida keys)
description: Medium-sized woodpecker that is not well named; rarely is the slight red wash on the belly visible! Instead, note the black-and-white barring on the back and wings, plain buffy breast and face, and red nape.

name: Oriole Blackbird
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to venezuela, the guianas, amazonian brazil, and northeastern peru
description: Beautiful and unmistakable: larger than most orioles, predominantly golden-yellow with black back, wings, and tail. Also note black surrounding eye and black mustache.

name: Black-crested Finch
rangeDescription: Chaco of southeastern bolivia to western paraguay and northern argentina
description: Striking and distinctive small finch-like tanager of the Chaco desert from central Argentina to W Paraguay and S Bolivia. Prefers open cactus and thorn woodland, often near roads and settlements.

name: Andean Slaty Thrush
rangeDescription: Breeds in the andes of southern bolivia (north to santa cruz) and northwestern argentina (southward to córdoba), also locally in southwestern ecuador and northwestern peru; nonbreeding migrant to the east slope of the andes from southeastern ecuador to bolivia
description: A distinctive gray thrush found in montane forests below around 2,000 m from Peru to Argentina. Males are medium-gray above and paler gray below with a darker head, lightly streaked throat, and a yellow bill and eyering.

name: Taita Fiscal
rangeDescription: Southeastern south sudan, northeastern uganda, ethiopia, somalia, kenya, and northeastern tanzania
description: A small black, white, and gray shrike. The sexes are similar, but females can show a small chestnut patch on the flanks.

name: Chestnut-colored Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Gulf-caribbean slope of southern mexico (southern veracruz) to western panama
description: Attractive, medium-sized crested woodpecker of humid tropical lowlands. Uncommon in evergreen forest and edge ranging into adjacent clearings with taller trees.

name: Tricolored Blackbird
rangeDescription: Marshes and farmlands of southwestern oregon to northwestern baja california
description: Very similar to Red-winged Blackbird. Male entirely glossy black with red shoulder patch bordered by white, not yellow.

name: Grenada Dove
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of southern grenada (southern lesser antilles)
description: A somewhat large, chunky dove of dry scrub woodlands where it is typically found foraging on ground. Its plain plumage, the lack of white on the wings, and the very limited white on its tail, distinguish it from other doves on Grenada.

name: Buru White-eye
rangeDescription: Mainly montane forest of buru (southern moluccas)
description: A small songbird with a prominent white eye-ring, a narrow yellow band on the forehead, green upperparts, a yellow rump, and an entirely yellow underside. Small groups roam the upper levels of forest, scrub, and patches of trees on farmland in the lowlands and foothills.
